name: Box (static liquid-nitrogen-vapour) freezing of bull semen straws: 10 min on a rack 4.5 cm above liquid nitrogen, then plunge into liquid nitrogen for storage
plain_name: Freeze bull semen straws on a rack held just above a pool of liquid nitrogen
description: The equipment-light alternative in the USDA ARS National Animal Germplasm Program bull-semen protocol (no programmable freezer): 0.5 mL straws on a rack are held in static liquid-nitrogen vapour 4.5 cm above the liquid surface for 10 min and then plunged into the liquid nitrogen, where they are stored at liquid-nitrogen temperature until thawing at 37 °C for insemination.
keywords: Freeze bull semen straws on a rack held just above a pool of liquid nitrogen

sources.citation: USDA ARS National Animal Germplasm Program: Bull Semen Collection, Transportation, Processing and Cryopreservation Protocol (2020)
Youngs CR (2011). Cryopreservation of preimplantation embryos of cattle, sheep, and goats. J Vis Exp (54): e2764. doi:10.3791/2764

reported_equipment: rack in liquid nitrogen vapor (4.5 cm above liquid nitrogen)

requirements.rationale: Freezing happens in the vapour 4.5 cm above a liquid-nitrogen pool and the straws are then plunged into the liquid nitrogen, so the container must hold liquid nitrogen.
The frozen straws end up immersed in liquid nitrogen, whose temperature the livestock-embryo protocol states as -196 °C (77.15 K); the storage space must reach it.
The straws are plunged directly into liquid nitrogen after vapour freezing; supporting flag only.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
